description: Questions about the running game: what is written on the screen, the scene tree, the nodes matching a query, where one node is on screen, what one property reads, the performance metrics, or what it tells a screen reader. Needs the game running with the runtime addon. Operations: tree: the live scene tree; text: every line of text under nodePath, the values in its fields included, in reading order, leaving out what is hidden and everything under it. Every line reads as drawn: rich text without tags, text only as far as it is typed out, a translation rather than its key, an upper-case label in capitals and a secret field as its mask. Tab titles, menu bar titles, list items, a tree's column titles and rows, and an open menu's items and the titles of its separators read a line each; find: the paths of every node matching className, script, namePattern, group or says, with property read off each, hidden ones included unless includeHidden says otherwise; rect (needs nodePath): one node's rectangle or position, in canvas and in window pixels. Canvas is the node's own viewport; window is where it is drawn in the game's window, through any embedded dialog or SubViewport it sits in, which is what runtime_input mouse_click and mouse_motion take. A 3D node answers with the point to aim at, which is the middle of what it draws rather than the origin it stands on, the rectangle it covers under covers, the camera that drew it, and behind_camera when it is not in front of one; property (needs nodePath, property): what one property reads on a node, or through the objects it holds, refusing a name nothing along the way has; metrics: frame time, memory, draw calls and the rest. frame_time is the mean wall time of the last frames_timed frames (up to 120; the game, physics and the wait for the display included), frame_time_max the slowest, both in seconds and null before a frame has passed; vsync says whether a frame waits for the display, and max_fps is the game's frame-rate cap, 0 for none. process_frames and physics_frames count frames and physics steps since the start; get_frames_drawn() stays 0 headless. physics_steps_per_second is the physics steps a second over those frames, fewer than physics_ticks_per_second when a frame needs more than max_physics_steps_per_frame or the editor's Game view slows it. fps, process_time_max and physics_time are the engine's monitors, set once a second: the last second's frames and its slowest process and physics step, so they trail a change by up to a second, and the last two are worst cases, not the frame. Memory, object and render counts are read as asked. memory_static is the engine's CPU-side allocation in bytes; render_video_mem_used, render_texture_mem_used and render_buffer_mem_used are the renderer's GPU memory in bytes, which memory_static leaves out; accessibility: what the game tells a screen reader, read through UI Automation as a Windows screen reader does, under windows: one tree per window, each element with its role (text for static text, button, check_box, group for a control holding others), name, value, value_text (a range's spoken words, such as "75%"), description, placeholder, bounds in the window's pixels, the actions a reader is offered (click, focus, toggle, set_value, select, expand_collapse, scroll_into_view), and focused on the focused one. node is the node that made the element; a part a node made of itself has part_of, the node drawn around it that holds its words, or part_of_candidates where several are, and part: announcement marks the text a window announces through. An empty name reads as nothing: static text takes it from accessibility_update_set_value, and _note counts the text elements on screen with none. tooltip is the node's tooltip_text, which a Windows reader is not told. With nothing focused, the engine calls GdharnessRuntime focused. Needs a windowed Windows run started with engineArgs ["--accessibility", "always"] or accessibility_support at Always Active, since the engine builds the tree only when asked; reading takes a second or two. Default tree.

className.description: find: a native class, matching its subclasses too, or a class_name. Only for op find.

depth.description: tree: levels to descend, 0 for the node alone. Default 3. Only for op tree.

group.description: find: a group the node is in. Only for op find.

includeHidden.description: text: read hidden nodes as well, for checking that something is not showing. Default false. find: default true, since a find means the node whether or not it is drawn; false answers with what the player can actually see, which is how a panel that keeps a label for every line and hides the ones that do not is read. A node counts as hidden when the engine would not draw it: a hidden Control, Node2D or Node3D above it hides it, a plain Node in between breaks that chain as it does for the engine, and a hidden canvas layer or window hides everything in it. How many matches were left out comes back under hidden. Only for ops text, find.

includeProperties.description: tree: include every stored property of each node. Default false, and one row of a form answered seventy-six thousand characters with it; properties names the few that are wanted. Only for op tree.

limit.description: find: the most nodes to answer with, default 100. text: the most lines, default 500, with omitted saying how many lines that left behind. accessibility: the most elements below the windows, depth first, with omitted counting the rest; default all. At most 5000 for either. A screen whose dialog sits under a long list is a screen read with omitted greater than zero, so raise this or point root at the dialog rather than reading the answer as what is on screen. Only for ops find, text, accessibility.

metrics.description: metrics: which to read. Default all. Only for op metrics.

namePattern.description: find: a case-insensitive glob on the node name, such as "Enemy*", or several separated by | the way says takes them, such as "Enemy*|Boss", with \| for a bar in a name. Matched against the whole name, so a bare word finds only a node called exactly that; an answer of none says how many names contain it and what glob would have found them. Only for op find.

nodePath.description: tree, find, text: where to start, default /root. rect: the node to place. property: the node to read, or an engine singleton by name as runtime_invoke takes them, "Engine" with property "get_frames_drawn()". accessibility: only the elements that node and those below it made, whether as node or part_of, each window keeping the outermost of them with what they hold, and matched counting them. What a ScrollContainer holds out of its sight is not in the tree until it is scrolled to, so an element missing under one may be scrolled away rather than hidden. Only for ops tree, text, find, rect, property, accessibility.

pid.description: Which game, when several are running from one project, such as a bench and its workers: its process id, as editor_status lists under runtimes. Without it the game this server started or plays is the one asked when it is among them, and the answer says so under answeredBy; with one game per project it is not needed at all.

projectPath.description: Which game, when more than one is running: the project directory it was started from. The pick without it, in order: the game this server started or is playing when it is among those running, named under answeredBy where there was a choice; else the only game there is; else a refusal naming every game and which argument tells them apart, pid when they are all one project and projectPath when they are not. Not needed with one game, nor for a call to this server's own.

properties.description: tree: the properties to read off each node, by name, so the text of every label and button under a panel is one call: a node that has not got one leaves it out. Colons read through what a node holds, as property does for find. accessibility: the fields to keep on each element, such as ["role", "name", "node"], leaving out the rest (bounds, actions, tooltip); children are always kept. Only for ops tree, accessibility.

property.description: property: which one to read. find: read this one off every node matched, so a panel of labels is one call rather than one per label. Colons read through what a node holds, "_game:clock:speed", which is where a game keeps what is worth asking about. A number or a key steps into a list or a map, "_game:run:roster:0:traits", which is how the lists a game keeps its state in are walked: a roster, a board, an in-tray. A key holding a colon, a bracket or a quote is written in double quotes, 'stock:"base:dew"', as a refusal listing the keys writes it. A packed list, such as a PackedStringArray, steps the same way. A negative number counts from the end. A vector, a colour, a rectangle or a transform is stepped into by its components as GDScript names them, so one axis is one number: "size:x", "global_position:y", "modulate:a", "global_transform:origin:z"; a name the value does not have is refused, naming the ones it has. A step written as a call, "get_viewport():gui_get_focus_owner()", calls a method that only reads (an engine method the engine marks as reading, or a game method not declared -> void, so queue_free() is refused) and walks into what it returned, which is how a question only a method answers is read in one call: which control holds the focus in the viewport this one is in. An engine method that reads takes literal arguments in its brackets, words in double quotes, numbers, true, false or null, so a control's theme is read where it is drawn: 'get_theme_stylebox("panel"):content_margin_top' or 'get_theme_constant("separation")'. A game method is given none in a path, since nothing marks one as only reading; runtime_invoke call takes those. A list or a map answers the calls that read it and take no arguments, "_game:run:board:size()" or "_game:inbox:keys()", and not those that change it, such as clear() or sort(). A step that is not there is named, and says what was there instead. Only for ops property, find.

says.description: accessibility: only the elements whose name, value or value_text says these words, matched as find matches them, with what they hold. find: part of what the node has written on it as drawn, the way the text op reads it, case-insensitively and with a typed space matching any space the game draws (a non-breaking one included), which is how a button is reached by the word on it rather than by a generated path. Its own text, so a row is found by the label in it, and hidden nodes match. A bare word is a contains; write a glob and it is one, matched against the whole of what the node says, the same as namePattern, and a glob that finds nothing says under note how many nodes it would find open at both ends. A label with a line break is matched with the break in the words, and a backslash followed by n counts as one. Alternatives separated by | match when any one of them does, each by these rules ("*won*|*lost*"); write \| for a bar that is part of the words. Only for ops find, accessibility.

script.description: find: the script file the node carries. Only for op find.

timeoutMs.description: How long to wait for the answer before answering pending with a requestId, which runtime_invoke op result collects the reply by. Default 10000, or GDHARNESS_RUNTIME_TIMEOUT_MS; accessibility defaults to 30000 or that, whichever is longer.

name: runtime_inspect
title: Inspect the running game
